name: 4D
tagline: French integrated database and app-development platform for desktop, client/server and web apps.
description: 4D (originally 4th Dimension) is a long-running platform from 4D SAS that bundles a relational database engine, a programming language, a form designer and an application server, so a small team can ship a complete desktop, client/server or web business application. Modern versions add ORDA (an object-relational data API), a REST server, project-mode source files suitable for Git, encryption and an AI kit with semantic ranking and local AI writing aids. It follows a yearly LTS plus quarterly feature-release model: 21 LTS arrived in January 2026 and 21 R4 in October 2026. It has a loyal ISV following, especially in Europe, but a small global community.

pricing.notes: Developer subscriptions plus server/user deployment licences; trial available.

scale.notes: Single 4D Server with many clients; backup/mirroring for availability.

strengths: Database, language, UI builder and app server in one product for small teams
Native macOS and Windows clients from one codebase, plus a REST/web server
ORDA gives an object API over relational tables
Predictable LTS plus quarterly feature-release cadence
Project mode stores code as text files that work with Git
weaknesses: Small developer community and job market
Proprietary language and runtime create lock-in
Not designed for horizontally scaled or high-traffic web services
useCases: Vertical ISV business applications for SMBs
Desktop client/server apps on mixed Mac and Windows fleets
Internal line-of-business tools with REST integrations
notIdealFor: Large-scale web or mobile back ends
Teams wanting mainstream languages and frameworks
